entries.evidence: Compatible with all computed stems and filtration restrictions; strongest classical spherical-class prediction.
entries.name: Curtis conjecture
entries.source: Curtis; Wellington; later work of Hung, Zare, Eccles
entries.statement: At p=2, the positive-dimensional spherical classes in H_*(Q_0 S^0;F_2) are exactly those arising from Hopf-invariant-one and Kervaire-invariant-one elements.

entries.evidence: Generalizes the Hopf/Kervaire detection philosophy.
entries.name: Eccles conjecture
entries.source: Eccles; expositions and partial verifications by Zare
entries.statement: For connected X, a positive-dimensional spherical class in H_*QX is either stably spherical or comes from a stable map detected by a primary operation in its mapping cone.
entries.status: open in general; verified in selected loop spaces

entries.evidence: Algebraic shadow of the Curtis conjecture; known nonzero cases occur in filtrations 1 and 2.
entries.name: Lannes-Zarati algebraic spherical-class conjecture
entries.source: Lannes-Zarati; Hung and collaborators
entries.statement: The s-th Lannes-Zarati homomorphism vanishes in every positive stem for s>2.
entries.status: open; proved in families and ranges

entries.evidence: Would make pi_* faithful on finite spectra; resisted all known approaches.
entries.name: Freyd generating hypothesis
entries.source: Freyd 1966
entries.statement: A map of finite spectra inducing zero on all stable homotopy groups is null.
entries.status: open globally; false in several localized/analogous categories

entries.evidence: Doomsday differentials on h_j^3 and the 2026 e-family theorem support it.
entries.name: New Doomsday conjecture
entries.source: Minami 1995; progress by Burklund-Xu and Li-Li
entries.statement: For every Adams filtration s there is an n(s) such that no nonzero class in the image of (Sq^0)^(n(s)) in the mod-two Adams E_2-page at filtration s is a permanent cycle.
entries.status: open in general; established for major low-filtration families including the e-family

entries.evidence: Organizes extensive EHP data but requires exceptions.
entries.name: Ravenel odd-primary EHP birth conjecture (Conj. 1.5.20)
entries.source: Ravenel 2026, Conjecture 1.5.20
entries.statement: Predicts the sphere of origin, EHP differentials, and Hopf invariants for divided alpha-family classes.
entries.status: not correct verbatim; Ravenel records an explicit p=3 exception; viable only after refinement

entries.evidence: Fits Mahowald-style EHP patterns.
entries.name: Ravenel EHP differential conjecture for eta_j (Conj. 1.5.26)
entries.source: Ravenel 2026, Conjecture 1.5.26
entries.statement: For k=(2s+1)2^{j-2}, s>0, the predicted EHP differential d_{2^{j-2}}(nu)=eta_j occurs.

entries.evidence: Low cases and classical EHP calculations.
entries.name: Kervaire EHP-pattern conjecture (Ravenel Conj. 1.5.27)
entries.source: Ravenel 2026; HHR; Lin-Wang-Xu
entries.statement: Predicts EHP behavior and spheres of origin for Kervaire classes theta_j.
entries.status: existence portion settled/refuted by dimension (theta_1...theta_6 only, with theta_6 currently a preprint theorem); differential pattern remains partly open

entries.evidence: Root-invariant and EHP calculations in low dimensions.
entries.name: Mahowald invariant of Kervaire classes
entries.source: Ravenel 2026, Conjecture 1.5.32
entries.statement: M(theta_j) contains theta_{j+1} whenever both classes exist.
entries.status: meaningful only for existing consecutive classes; partially verified

entries.evidence: Captures observed redshift of root invariants.
entries.name: Chromatic Mahowald/root-invariant conjecture
entries.source: Ravenel 2026, Conjecture 1.5.33
entries.statement: When consecutive Greek-letter classes alpha_j^(n) and alpha_j^(n+1) exist, the higher-height class lies in the Mahowald invariant of the lower-height class.
entries.status: open; many low-height examples and motivic/root-invariant calculations

entries.evidence: Fits the complete p=5 calculation and chromatic heuristics.
entries.name: Ravenel beta_1 exponent conjecture at p>=7 (Conj. 7.6.2)
entries.source: Ravenel 2026, Conjecture 7.6.2
entries.statement: For p>=7, beta_1^(p^2-p) is nonzero, beta_1^(p^2-p+1) vanishes, and <gamma_3,gamma_2,...,gamma_2>, with gamma_2 repeated (p-5)/2 times, equals beta_1^((2p-1)(p-1)/2).
entries.status: open for p>=7; p=5 analogue computed with beta_1^17 nonzero and beta_1^18 killed

entries.evidence: Survives after stronger decompositional forms fail.
entries.name: Chromatic splitting conjecture - weak form
entries.source: Hovey 1995, Introduction p. 2 and Conjecture 4.2(v)
entries.statement: For every prime p, height n>=1, and finite spectrum X, L_(n-1) of the p-completion of X is a wedge summand of L_(n-1)L_K(n) of the p-completion of X.
entries.status: open in general; known at n=1 and several height-2 odd-prime cases

entries.evidence: Beaudry produced a contradiction to the strongest Hovey formulation.
entries.name: Chromatic splitting conjecture - strongest classical decomposition
entries.source: Beaudry 2015
entries.statement: A precise wedge decomposition of lower chromatic localizations of the K(n)-local sphere.
entries.status: false at n=p=2; refined variants remain open

entries.evidence: Hahn-Wilson, Clausen-Mathew-Naumann-Noel, and subsequent work prove broad forms and bounds.
entries.name: Redshift conjecture
entries.source: Ausoni-Rognes and recent redshift theorems
entries.statement: Algebraic K-theory of a suitably height-n ring spectrum exhibits height n+1 phenomena, together with corresponding descent properties.
entries.status: major upper-bound and many positive cases proved; full lower-bound/descent package open

entries.evidence: Includes odd-sphere exponent theorems as central evidence.
entries.name: Moore conjecture on homotopy exponents
entries.source: J. C. Moore; Selick; modern exponent literature
entries.statement: A finite simply connected CW complex has a finite p-primary homotopy exponent iff its rational homotopy is finite-dimensional (rationally elliptic).
entries.status: open in general; many elliptic families and special classes proved

entries.evidence: All computed Kervaire-Milnor groups support the list.
entries.name: Unique smooth sphere conjecture
entries.source: Isaksen-Wang-Xu, Conjecture 2.2
entries.statement: Among n>4, the only dimensions with a unique smooth structure on S^n are 5,6,12,56,61.
entries.status: open; verified through the current low-stem range

entries.evidence: Stable coker-J detections and recent eta-torsion families.
entries.name: Very exotic sphere conjecture
entries.source: Bobkova-Quigley and related geometric applications
entries.statement: Very exotic spheres exist in every dimension >4 except 5,6,11,12,27,43,56,61.
entries.status: open; new 192-periodic constructions prove infinite congruence classes

entries.evidence: Separate from stable-stem methods and high-dimensional surgery.
entries.name: Smooth 4-dimensional Poincare conjecture
entries.source: classical smooth 4-manifold problem
entries.statement: Every smooth homotopy 4-sphere is diffeomorphic to S^4.

entries.evidence: Carrick-Davies confirm a large collection, including tmf-invisible families.
entries.name: Hopkins-Mahowald height-two family predictions
entries.source: Hopkins-Mahowald charts; Carrick-Davies
entries.statement: Predicts specific 192-periodic height-two families and orders in congruence classes modulo 192.
entries.status: many predictions confirmed; catalog not known to be exhaustive

entries.evidence: The counterexample claims are recent preprints and should be independently audited; the unqualified global conjecture should no longer be presented as a credible open prediction.
entries.name: Singer algebraic transfer conjecture
entries.source: Singer; Sum arXiv:2408.06669; Phuc arXiv:2509.09455v11; rank-4 positive results
entries.statement: Singer conjectured that the mod-2 algebraic transfer is injective (monic) in every rank and degree.
entries.status: original global conjecture is challenged/refuted by current preprints claiming counterexamples in ranks 5 and 6; low-rank and degreewise injectivity results remain valid

entries.evidence: Burklund-Senger upper bounds and chromatic heuristics.
entries.name: Asymptotic stable-stem growth sharpness scenario
entries.source: Burklund-Senger
entries.statement: A strong form of telescope failure would make the exp(Theta((log n)^3)) upper-scale for cumulative Adams data essentially sharp for stable stems.
entries.status: conditional prediction, not a standard named conjecture

entries.evidence: No longer listed as a credible open conjecture at height >=2.
entries.name: Telescope conjecture
entries.source: Burklund-Hahn-Levy-Schlank
entries.statement: T(n)-localization and K(n)-localization agree on spectra of chromatic height n.
entries.status: historical conjecture; preprint theorem gives counterexamples at every prime and every height >=2; true at heights 0 and 1

entries.evidence: Retained only as historical status, not a credible conjecture.
entries.name: Kervaire invariant one in dimensions beyond 126
entries.source: HHR; Lin-Wang-Xu
entries.statement: Historical prediction that further theta_j might exist.
entries.status: refuted for j>=7 by Hill-Hopkins-Ravenel; theta_6 existence is a current preprint theorem

entries.evidence: Useful organizing principle, but not a precise falsifiable statement.
entries.name: Mahowald uncertainty principle
entries.source: Mahowald/Ravenel expository tradition
entries.statement: Heuristic tradeoff: classes easy to detect chromatically tend to be hard to construct geometrically, and vice versa.

entries.evidence: Odd-primary Dyer-Lashof structure and Adams-filtration constraints parallel the 2-primary Curtis philosophy, but the correct final formulation is less settled.
entries.name: Odd-primary spherical-class conjectures
entries.source: Eccles, Wellington, Zare, and odd-primary spherical-class literature
entries.statement: At an odd prime, positive-dimensional spherical classes in the homology of Q_0S^0 should be restricted to the corresponding low-filtration Hopf/J and exceptional chromatic detections, with no large unexplained families.
entries.status: no single universally accepted formulation; several precise variants and partial vanishing theorems

entries.evidence: The p=5 beta_1-power computation gives sharp nonexistence information; periodicity theory supplies existence after weakening the precise Smith-Toda form.
entries.name: Smith-Toda complex existence pattern
entries.source: Ravenel 2026, Theorem 7.6.1; Smith-Toda and Hopkins-Smith literature
entries.statement: For a prime p and height n, one seeks finite type-n complexes V(n) with BP-homology BP_*/(p,v_1,...,v_n), subject to prime-size constraints; broad existence/nonexistence patterns are expected but not known uniformly.
entries.status: case-by-case; V(3) does not exist at p=5 and V(2) is not a ring spectrum there; higher cases remain incomplete

entries.evidence: Stable chromatic families and rational/elliptic-hyperbolic dichotomies suggest structured growth, while current finite tables are too short to identify a law.
entries.name: Sharp unstable homotopy growth conjectures
entries.source: Burklund-Senger; Boyde; rational homotopy hyperbolicity literature
entries.statement: For a fixed sphere, the p-primary ranks and total torsion should exhibit explicit chromatic growth laws substantially sharper than the current exp(O((log n)^3)) upper bounds.
entries.status: open; several hyperbolicity and lower-bound results, but no sharp general asymptotic

high_dimensional_results.result: Complete additive stable homotopy groups, all primes and additive extensions.
Exact in stems 87, 88, 89; explicit alternatives remain in stems 84, 85, 86, 90.
Complete p-local additive groups from the non-J table plus the all-dimensional image of J.
Ravenel table records all non-J classes/relations through stem 999; source question marks are preserved at 932, 933, 970, 971; add image J by closed formula.
high_dimensional_results.status: author-maintained digital monograph revision; four marked uncertainties/identification questions

high_dimensional_results.result: The odd-primary image of J is cyclic of order p^(1+v_p(t)) in stem 2(p-1)t-1 and zero otherwise.
Full v1-periodic summands follow the 8-periodic bo/J pattern, with cyclic orders controlled by the 2-adic valuation in stems 8t-1.
The class h_6^2 is claimed to survive, giving theta_6 and a Kervaire-invariant-one element in stem 126.
125 explicit v_2^32-periodic families; seven simple order-4 families and four simple order-8 families; all tmf-invisible and detected by an Atkin-Lehner fixed-point spectrum.
Seven order-2 periodic families survive T(2)- and K(2)-localization.
Five simple eta-torsion families with trivial tmf Hurewicz image; additional tmf-detected families are proved simple eta-torsion.
Many products among divided beta families are nonzero; selected Toda brackets exclude zero; the connective height-two image-of-J spectrum j_2 detects the classes.
Every fivefold product in the family beta_{1+9s} is nonzero and every sixfold product is zero; extensions to other families.
beta_1^17 is nonzero and beta_1^18 is killed by d_33(gamma_3); consequently V(3) does not exist and V(2) is not a ring spectrum at p=5.
A uniform d_4 differential kills the h_j^3 family; h_j^2 survives to E_5.
The New Doomsday conjecture is established for the e-family on the Adams 4-line using the Burklund-Xu spectral sequence and Bruner formulas.
high_dimensional_results.source: Runji Li and Yuxuan Li, Proceedings of the AMS, DOI 10.1090/proc/17823

high_dimensional_results.result: T(n)- and K(n)-localization are claimed not to agree: counterexamples to the telescope conjecture at every prime and every height at least two.
The p-exponent grows sublinearly; the Adams E_2 p-rank has exp(Theta((log n)^3)) growth; stable stems admit the first general subexponential size bound.
All groups pi_{n+k}(S^n), all primes and extensions, are completely determined.
Complete all-sphere 2-primary groups through the 32-stem after later corrections.
Known for n=2,...,9 and n>=28; n=10,...,26 unresolved; n=27 is source-internally inconsistent. Three 2026 groups: pi_39(S^6)_2=Z/4+(Z/2)^6, pi_40(S^7)_2=Z/4+(Z/2)^4, pi_41(S^8)_2=Z/8+Z/4+(Z/2)^6.
high_dimensional_results.status: broader three-group source is a 2024 preprint; published predecessor components

high_dimensional_results.result: Complete prime-local tables across all sphere dimensions in the stated range.

high_dimensional_results.degrees: all m>=2 for S^2 and m>=3 for S^3
high_dimensional_results.result: No positive-degree unstable homotopy group of S^2 or S^3 vanishes.
high_dimensional_results.source: Ivanov-Mikhailov-Wu; Hopf fibration transfer to S^3

records.claim_scope: The classical mod-2 Adams spectral sequence for the sphere spectrum, with implemented E3-page data through stable stem 140 and all previously unknown d2, d3, d4, and d5 differentials resolved through stable stem 95.
records.lattice_reason: A spectral-sequence-page and differential computation is input to stable-stem calculations, not by itself a complete integral additive-group row.
records.publication_status: arXiv v2 preprint and 2022 Harvard PhD dissertation
records.result: Computed Adams E3-page data and low-page differentials
records.source_locator: Abstract and Introduction, part 2 and part 3 summaries
records.statement: Chua gives an algorithm for every Adams d2 and the filtration-one hidden extensions on E3, implements the E3-page computation through stem 140, and uses those extensions to resolve the remaining d2 through d5 differentials through stem 95.
records.work_title: The E3 page of the Adams spectral sequence

records.claim_scope: At every prime p, the unit from the sphere spectrum to the connective image-of-J spectrum j at p, in every homotopy degree.
records.lattice_reason: Surjective detection of height-one classes does not determine the full ambient integral stable homotopy group in any new stem.
records.publication_status: peer-reviewed publication, Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 379 (2026), 1985-2031
records.result: All-degree detection by the connective image-of-J spectrum
records.source_locator: Theorem A and the paragraph immediately following it
records.statement: For each prime p, the unit S -> j is surjective on homotopy groups in every degree. The Adams e-invariant splits the degreewise surjection; the paper also gives filtered refinements.
records.work_title: A synthetic approach to detecting v1-periodic families

records.claim_scope: The vn^{-1}BP-local sphere LnS^0 at a prime p when n^2 <= 2p-1, excluding (p,n)=(2,1) and (3,2), together with the exceptional gamma and delta cases in Theorem 1.3.
records.lattice_reason: The theorem is about Bousfield-localized sphere spectra and does not assert that the localized classes lift to the integral stable stems.
records.result: Greek-letter families in localized sphere spectra
records.statement: For every nonzero integer s under the stated hypotheses, the nth Greek-letter element alpha_s^(n) is a permanent cycle and generates a Z/p submodule of pi_*(LnS^0). In particular, the paper obtains gamma_s at (p,n)=(5,3), delta_s at (7,4), and order-p delta_s in pi_*(L4S^0) for p >= 7.
records.work_title: A note on the Greek letter elements of the homotopy of the Ln-local spheres

records.claim_scope: Stable integral homology of the infinite symmetric group and the basepoint component of the infinite loop space underlying the sphere spectrum.
records.lattice_reason: This is a foundational model for stable homotopy, not a computation of any particular integral group.
records.publication_status: foundational peer-reviewed theorem, Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici 47 (1972), 1-14
records.source_locator: Equation (1.2) and Section 4; modern exact formulation in Delarue, Theorem 1.1
records.statement: There is an integral homology equivalence B Sigma_infinity -> Omega^infinity_0 S. Equivalently after the Quillen plus construction, this supplies the standard bridge from stable symmetric groups to the basepoint component of QS^0.
records.work_title: On the Homology of Non-Connected Monoids and Their Associated Groups

records.claim_scope: Non-bp homotopy spheres with nontrivial 2- or 3-local Pontryagin-Thom invariant, in the dimension families of Theorem A.
records.lattice_reason: Existence of exotic smooth structures and free actions is a geometric consequence of selected stable classes, not a complete additive-group calculation.
records.result: Infinite families of very exotic spheres with free circle and 3-sphere actions
records.statement: For every k >= 0 there are non-bp spheres in dimensions 15+96k (nontrivial 2-local invariant) and 13+72k (nontrivial 3-local invariant) with smooth free S^1-actions. There are also non-bp spheres with nontrivial 2-local invariant and smooth free S^3-actions in dimension 35+96k, in one of dimensions 15+96k or 11+96k, and in one of dimensions 59+96k or 55+96k.
records.work_title: Infinite families of very exotic spheres with free S1- and S3-actions

records.claim_scope: Named stable 24-stem Toda brackets and specified unstable composites in pi_30(S^6) and pi_31(S^7).
records.lattice_reason: These are named bracket and composition relations inside already-covered groups; they do not change an additive-group value or its exactness status.
records.result: Nonzero 24-stem Toda brackets and unstable relations
records.statement: The stable brackets <bar-nu,sigma,bar-nu> and <nu,eta,bar-sigma> are the same nonzero class eta eta* sigma, settling the cited Mahowald conjecture. The paper also determines bar-nu_6 omega_14 modulo its stated indeterminacy and proves bar-nu_7 omega_15 = nu_7 sigma_10 kappa_17.
records.work_title: Relations in the 24-th homotopy groups of spheres
